    }
}

contract RaffleDosTest is Test {
    Raffle public raffle;
    MockSpin public spin;
    address public admin = address(0xADMIN);
    address public supraRouterAddress = address(0xSUPRA);

    bytes32 public constant SUPRA_ROLE = keccak256("SUPRA_ROLE");

    function setUp() public {
        vm.startPrank(admin);
        spin = new MockSpin();
        raffle = new Raffle();
        raffle.initialize(address(spin), supraRouterAddress);
        raffle.grantRole(SUPRA_ROLE, supraRouterAddress);
        vm.stopPrank();
    }

    function test_handlesWinnerSelection_reverts_on_empty_rng() public {
        // Admin creates prize and user buys ticket
        vm.startPrank(admin);
        raffle.addPrize("Prize", "desc", 1 ether, 1);
        uint256 prizeId = 1;
        vm.stopPrank();

        address user = address(1);
        spin.grantRaffleTickets(user, 1);
        vm.prank(user);
        raffle.spendRaffle(prizeId, 1);

        // Forge-set internal mappings to mimic a pending request
        uint256 requestId = 123;
        bytes32 pendingSlot = keccak256(abi.encode(requestId, uint256(10))); // slot 10 = pendingVRFRequests
        vm.store(address(raffle), pendingSlot, bytes32(prizeId));
        bytes32 pendingFlagSlot = keccak256(abi.encode(prizeId, uint256(11))); // slot 11 = isWinnerRequestPending
        vm.store(address(raffle), pendingFlagSlot, bytes32(uint256(1)));

        // Call with empty RNG array via Supra role
        vm.startPrank(supraRouterAddress);
        uint256[] memory emptyRng = new uint256[](0);
        vm.expectRevert();
        raffle.handleWinnerSelection(requestId, emptyRng);
        vm.stopPrank();
    }
}

## Suggested Mitigation
Add a requirement at the beginning of the `handleWinnerSelection` function to ensure the `rng` array has at least one element.

```solidity
function handleWinnerSelection(uint256 requestId, uint256[] memory rng) external override onlyRole(SUPRA_ROLE) {
    require(rng.length > 0, "RNG array is empty");
    uint256 prizeId = pendingVRFRequests[requestId];
    // ... rest of the function
}
```

## [M-25]. Gas Grief BlockLimit issue in Raffle::removePrize, getPrizeDetails, getPrizeWinners, getUserWinnings

## Description
The `removePrize` function and several getter functions (`getPrizeDetails`, `getPrizeWinners`, `getUserWinnings`) contain unbounded loops or return unbounded arrays. If the `prizeIds` array or other data arrays grow very large, transactions calling these functions can run out of gas, leading to a Denial of Service (DoS). An admin may be unable to remove a prize, and frontends may be unable to retrieve prize or winner data.

## Impact
No user funds can be stolen, but once the prize list grows large enough the ADMIN is unable to deactivate or edit prizes because `removePrize()` can no longer finish within the block gas limit. In addition, UI / indexers that rely on `getPrizeDetails`, `getPrizeWinners`, or `getUserWinnings` will revert, effectively freezing visibility of the raffle. This constitutes a permanent loss of liveness and governance over the raffle module even though funds remain in the contract.

## Proof of Concept
1. Assume the raffle has been running for months and currently stores 12,000 prizes (this is roughly the point where `removePrize()` requires ~29 M gas – close to the 30 M block limit on main-net).
2. The admin wants to deactivate the very first prize (id 1).
3. They broadcast the transaction:

```
raffle.removePrize{gas:30_000_000}(1);
```

4. The function iterates linearly over `prizeIds` (12,000 iterations) and consumes ~29 M gas just to find the index, plus another ~0.4 M for the storage writes.
5. The call runs out of gas and reverts – no matter how much gas the sender attaches, the hard block limit prevents success.
6. Because the prize remains active, users can still spend tickets on it but it can never be removed or edited.
7. Any front-end that calls `getPrizeDetails()` (which loops over the same 12,000 entries and materialises them in memory) will revert inside an `eth_call`, breaking the UI.

## Proof of Code
// SPDX-License-Identifier: UNLICENSED
pragma solidity ^0.8.20;

import "forge-std/Test.sol";
import {Raffle} from "src/spin/Raffle.sol";

// Minimal mocks
contract MockSpin { function getUserData(address) external pure returns (uint256,uint256,uint256,uint256,uint256,uint256,uint256){return(0,0,0,0,1e9,0,0);} function spendRaffleTickets(address,uint256) external {} }
contract MockSupra { function generateRequest(string calldata,uint8,uint256,uint256,address) external pure returns(uint256){return 1;} function generateRequest(string calldata,uint8,uint256,address) external pure returns(uint256){return 1;} }

contract GasGriefTest is Test {
    Raffle raffle;

    function setUp() public {
        raffle = new Raffle();
        raffle.initialize(address(new MockSpin()), address(new MockSupra()));
    }

    function _bulkInsert(uint256 n) internal {
        // populate with N prizes so that loops become expensive
        for (uint256 i; i < n; ++i) {
            raffle.addPrize(string(abi.encodePacked("P", vm.toString(i))), "d", 1, 1);
        }
    }

    function test_adminCannotRemoveWhenLarge() public {
        uint256 prizeCount = 12000; // ≈ block-limit threshold
        _bulkInsert(prizeCount);

        // Expect the call to run out of gas when we artificially cap gas below the block limit
        bytes memory callData = abi.encodeWithSelector(Raffle.removePrize.selector, 1);
        (bool success,) = address(raffle).call{gas: 29_500_000}(callData);
        assertTrue(!success, "call should fail due to OOG");
    }

    function test_viewRevertsWhenLarge() public {
        uint256 prizeCount = 12000;
        _bulkInsert(prizeCount);

        bytes memory callData = abi.encodeWithSelector(Raffle.getPrizeDetails.selector);
        (bool success,) = address(raffle).staticcall{gas: 29_500_000}(callData);
        assertTrue(!success, "eth_call should fail due to OOG");
    }
}

## Suggested Mitigation
For functions involving loops, replace iteration with direct access using mappings. For functions returning arrays, implement pagination.

1.  **For `removePrize`**: Use a mapping to track the index of each prize ID, allowing for O(1) removal.

    ```solidity
    mapping(uint256 => uint256) private prizeIdToIndex;

    function removePrize(uint256 prizeId) public {
        uint256 index = prizeIdToIndex[prizeId];
        uint256 lastId = prizeIds[prizeIds.length - 1];
        prizeIds[index] = lastId;
        prizeIdToIndex[lastId] = index;
        prizeIds.pop();
        delete prizeIdToIndex[prizeId];
    }
    ```

2.  **For Getter Functions**: Add pagination parameters (`cursor`/`offset`, `limit`).

    ```solidity
    function getPrizeDetails(uint256 cursor, uint256 limit) external view returns (PrizeWithTickets[] memory prizes, uint256 nextCursor) {
        uint256 length = prizeIds.length;
        uint256 to = cursor + limit;
        if (to > length) {
            to = length;
        }
        if (cursor >= to) {
            return (new PrizeWithTickets[](0), length);
        }
        // ... logic to return a slice of the prizes
        return (prizeSlice, to);
    }
    ```

## [M-26]. DOS issue in Raffle::claimPrize

## Description
The `claimPrize` function contains a logic flaw that prevents winners from claiming their prize until all winners for that specific prize have been drawn. The check `if (prizes[prizeId].isActive && winnersDrawn[prizeId] < prizes[prizeId].quantity)` will revert for any winner as long as not all prize quantities have been awarded. `prizes[prizeId].isActive` is only set to `false` in `handleWinnerSelection` when `winnersDrawn[prizeId] == prizes[prizeId].quantity`. This effectively creates a temporary Denial of Service against winners, blocking them from accessing their winnings.

## Impact
Legitimate winners are unable to claim their prizes for an indefinite period, until the raffle for that prize concludes entirely. This damages user trust and locks up winner assets.

## Proof of Concept
1. Admin creates a prize with a quantity greater than 1 (e.g., 5).
2. Users enter the raffle.
3. Admin calls `requestWinner`, and the first winner is selected via `handleWinnerSelection`. `winnersDrawn` becomes 1.
4. The prize remains active (`isActive == true`) because `winnersDrawn < quantity`.
5. The winner attempts to call `claimPrize`.
6. The transaction reverts because the condition `prizes[prizeId].isActive && winnersDrawn[prizeId] < prizes[prizeId].quantity` evaluates to `true`.

## Proof of Code
// SPDX-License-Identifier: UNLICENSED
pragma solidity 0.8.20;

import "forge-std/Test.sol";
import {Raffle} from "../../src/spin/Raffle.sol";

// -------------------------------------------------------------
// Minimal interfaces & mocks
// -------------------------------------------------------------
interface ISpinMock {
    function getUserData(address user) external view returns (uint256,uint256,uint256,uint256,uint256,uint256,uint256);
    function spendRaffleTickets(address user, uint256 amount) external;
}

contract MockSpin is ISpinMock {
    mapping(address => uint256) public tickets;

    constructor(address u1, uint256 t1, address u2, uint256 t2) {
        tickets[u1] = t1;
        tickets[u2] = t2;
    }

    function getUserData(address user)
        external
        view
        override
        returns (
            uint256,uint256,uint256,uint256,uint256,uint256,uint256
        )
    {
        return (0,0,0,0,tickets[user],0,0); // only 5th value is used by Raffle
    }

    function spendRaffleTickets(address user, uint256 amount) external override {
        require(tickets[user] >= amount, "insufficient");
        tickets[user] -= amount;
    }
}

interface ISupraRouterContract {
    function generateRequest(
        string calldata,
        uint8,
        uint256,
        uint256,
        address
    ) external returns (uint256);
}

contract MockSupraRouter is ISupraRouterContract {
    Raffle raffle;
    uint256 nonce;

    constructor(address _raffle) { raffle = Raffle(_raffle); }

    function generateRequest(
        string calldata,
        uint8,
        uint256,
        uint256,
        address
    ) external override returns (uint256 requestId) {
        requestId = ++nonce; // start from 1
        uint256[] memory rng = new uint256[](1);
        rng[0] = 0; // deterministic -> winningTicketIndex = 1
        raffle.handleWinnerSelection(requestId, rng);
    }
}

// -------------------------------------------------------------
// Test
// -------------------------------------------------------------
contract ClaimPrizeDOSTest is Test {
    Raffle raffle;
    MockSpin spin;
    MockSupraRouter supraRouter;

    address admin = address(0xA);
    address user1 = address(0x1);
    address user2 = address(0x2);

    uint256 constant PRIZE_ID = 1;

    function setUp() public {
        // deploy mocks
        spin = new MockSpin(user1, 10, user2, 10);
        raffle = new Raffle();
        supraRouter = new MockSupraRouter(address(raffle));

        // initialise raffle
        vm.prank(admin);
        raffle.initialize(address(spin), address(supraRouter));

        // add prize with 2 available winners
        vm.prank(admin);
        raffle.addPrize("Hat", "Cool hat", 1 ether, 2);

        // both users buy 1 ticket each
        vm.prank(user1);
        raffle.spendRaffle(PRIZE_ID, 1);
        vm.prank(user2);
        raffle.spendRaffle(PRIZE_ID, 1);

        // draw the first winner (user1 will win because rng==0 -> ticket index 1)
        vm.prank(admin);
        raffle.requestWinner(PRIZE_ID);
    }

    function test_DoS_on_first_winner_claim() public {
        // sanity: only 1 winner drawn & prize still active
        assertEq(raffle.winnersDrawn(PRIZE_ID), 1);
        assertTrue(raffle.prizes(PRIZE_ID).isActive());

        // user1 (valid winner) tries to claim but should revert
        vm.prank(user1);
        vm.expectRevert("WinnerNotDrawn()");
        raffle.claimPrize(PRIZE_ID, 0);
    }
}


## Suggested Mitigation
Remove the flawed conditional check at the beginning of the `claimPrize` function. The subsequent checks correctly validate if the caller is a winner and has not already claimed the prize.

```solidity
function claimPrize(uint256 prizeId, uint256 winnerIndex) external {
    // REMOVE THIS FAULTY CHECK:
    /*
    if (prizes[prizeId].isActive && winnersDrawn[prizeId] < prizes[prizeId].quantity) {
        revert WinnerNotDrawn();
    }
    */
    
    // Add a bounds check for winnerIndex
    require(winnerIndex < prizeWinners[prizeId].length, "Raffle: Invalid winner index");

    Winner storage individualWin = prizeWinners[prizeId][winnerIndex];

    if (individualWin.claimed) {
        revert WinnerClaimed();
    }
    if (msg.sender != individualWin.winnerAddress) {
        revert NotAWinner();
    }

    individualWin.claimed = true;
    winnings[msg.sender].push(prizeId);

    emit PrizeClaimed(msg.sender, prizeId, winnerIndex);
}
```

## [M-27]. Upgradeability Initializer Safety issue in Raffle::_authorizeUpgrade

## Description
The `_authorizeUpgrade` function, which is critical for the UUPS upgrade pattern, is protected by `onlyRole(ADMIN_ROLE)`. The `ADMIN_ROLE` is also used for day-to-day operational tasks such as adding and removing prizes. This violates the principle of least privilege by granting a single role both operational and ultimate administrative power. A compromised admin key would allow an attacker to perform a malicious upgrade, giving them complete control over the contract logic and any associated assets.

## Impact
Because the same ADMIN_ROLE is used for routine prize-management functions and for authorising proxy upgrades, any account that legitimately receives ADMIN_ROLE for operational purposes (or whose key is later compromised) can deploy a new implementation and upgrade the proxy to arbitrary logic. This escalates an "ordinary" admin permission (editing prizes, requesting winners, etc.) into full control over all storage and funds held by the contract.

## Proof of Concept
1. A legitimate operator is granted `ADMIN_ROLE` so that they can add and edit prizes.
2. The operator (or anyone who steals the operator’s key) deploys a malicious implementation contract.
3. The attacker calls `upgradeTo()` on the Raffle proxy from the compromised admin account.
4. `_authorizeUpgrade` passes because caller holds `ADMIN_ROLE`.
5. Proxy now points to attacker logic – the attacker can run arbitrary code, drain tokens, or brick the contract.

## Proof of Code
// SPDX-License-Identifier: UNLICENSED
pragma solidity ^0.8.20;

import "forge-std/Test.sol";
import {ERC1967Proxy} from "@openzeppelin/contracts/proxy/ERC1967/ERC1967Proxy.sol";
import {Raffle} from "src/spin/Raffle.sol";

contract MaliciousRaffle is Raffle {
    // new state variable proving storage collision is possible
    uint256 public hacked;

    function initializeMalicious() external {
        hacked = 0xdeadbeef;
    }

    function rug() external {
        hacked = 0x1;
    }

    // keep same auth semantics so upgrade is allowed for ADMIN_ROLE
    function _authorizeUpgrade(address) internal override onlyRole(ADMIN_ROLE) {}
}

contract UpgradeabilityTest is Test {
    address admin = vm.addr(1);
    Raffle proxy;

    function setUp() public {
        // deploy V1 implementation
        Raffle implV1 = new Raffle();
        // prepare initialization calldata
        bytes memory data = abi.encodeCall(Raffle.initialize, (address(0), address(0)));
        // deploy proxy pointing to V1
        ERC1967Proxy p = new ERC1967Proxy(address(implV1), data);
        proxy = Raffle(address(p));
        // give the admin some ether for tx fees
        vm.deal(admin, 1 ether);
    }

    function testAdminCanUpgrade() public {
        // deploy malicious implementation
        MaliciousRaffle implMalicious = new MaliciousRaffle();

        // upgrade via compromised admin
        vm.prank(admin);
        proxy.upgradeTo(address(implMalicious));

        // interact through the proxy with the new interface
        MaliciousRaffle upgraded = MaliciousRaffle(address(proxy));
        vm.prank(admin);
        upgraded.initializeMalicious();
        assertEq(upgraded.hacked(), 0xdeadbeef, "Upgrade succeeded and malicious state modified");
    }
}

## Suggested Mitigation
Follow the principle of least privilege by creating a separate, highly-secured `UPGRADER_ROLE` for authorizing contract upgrades. This role should be distinct from the operational `ADMIN_ROLE` and ideally managed by a secure multisig wallet or a DAO with a timelock.

```diff
contract Raffle is Initializable, UUPSUpgradeable, AccessControlUpgradeable {
    // ...
+   bytes32 public constant UPGRADER_ROLE = keccak256("UPGRADER_ROLE");

    function initialize(address _spinContract, address _supraRouter) public initializer {
        // ...
        _grantRole(ADMIN_ROLE, msg.sender);
+       _grantRole(UPGRADER_ROLE, msg.sender); // Or a different, more secure address
        // ...
    }

-   function _authorizeUpgrade(address /*newImplementation*/) internal override onlyRole(ADMIN_ROLE) {}
+   function _authorizeUpgrade(address /*newImplementation*/) internal override onlyRole(UPGRADER_ROLE) {}

    // ...
}
```

## [M-28]. Pausable Emergency Stop issue in Raffle::claimPrize

## Description
The `claimPrize` function contains a flawed check: `if (prizes[prizeId].isActive && winnersDrawn[prizeId] < prizes[prizeId].quantity) { revert WinnerNotDrawn(); }`. This logic incorrectly prevents a winner from claiming their prize until *all* winners for that prize have been drawn and the prize is consequently marked as inactive. This creates a situation where rewards are locked and inaccessible to the rightful winners for an extended period, leading to a severe user experience issue and breaking the core functionality of the contract.

## Impact
Because `claimPrize` reverts while `prizes[prizeId].isActive` is true, every winner is blocked from claiming until the *last* winner for that prize is drawn and the prize is de-activated. In practice this creates a permanent denial-of-service if the admin forgets or is unable to draw the remaining winners, breaking the core business logic and preventing users from receiving their prizes.

## Proof of Concept
1. Admin deploys Raffle and adds a prize with quantity=2.
2. Two users spend tickets to enter.
3. Admin draws only the first winner (UserA).
4. UserA immediately calls `claimPrize(prizeId,0)`.
5. The call reverts with the custom error `WinnerNotDrawn` because `isActive==true` and `winnersDrawn < quantity`.
6. Until the admin successfully draws the second winner, every call to `claimPrize` will keep reverting, effectively locking the prize.

No special privileges are required – the bug is hit under normal, honest use.

## Proof of Code
// SPDX-License-Identifier: UNLICENSED
pragma solidity ^0.8.20;

import "forge-std/Test.sol";
import {Raffle} from "src/spin/Raffle.sol";
import {ISpin} from "src/interfaces/ISpin.sol";
import {ISupraRouterContract} from "src/interfaces/ISupraRouterContract.sol";

/* ------------------ Mocks ------------------ */
contract MockSpin is ISpin {
    mapping(address => uint256) private _tickets;
    function setTickets(address user, uint256 amt) external { _tickets[user] = amt; }
    function getUserData(address user) external view returns (uint256,uint256,uint256,uint256,uint256,uint256,uint256){
        return (0,0,0,0,_tickets[user],0,0);
    }
    function spendRaffleTickets(address user, uint256 amt) external { _tickets[user] -= amt; }
}

contract MockSupraRouter is ISupraRouterContract {
    uint256 private _nonce;
    function generateRequest(string calldata,uint8,uint8,uint256,address) external returns(uint256){
        _nonce += 1; return _nonce; }
}

/* ------------------ Test ------------------ */
contract ClaimLockTest is Test {
    Raffle raffle;
    MockSpin spin;
    MockSupraRouter router;
    address admin = address(1);
    address user1 = address(2);
    address user2 = address(3);

    function setUp() public {
        spin   = new MockSpin();
        router = new MockSupraRouter();

        vm.prank(admin);
        raffle = new Raffle();
        raffle.initialize(address(spin), address(router));
        vm.prank(admin);
        raffle.grantRole(raffle.SUPRA_ROLE(), address(router));

        // create prize with two winners
        vm.prank(admin);
        raffle.addPrize("Two-winner prize", "", 0, 2);

        // give tickets and enter raffle
        spin.setTickets(user1, 1);
        vm.prank(user1);
        raffle.spendRaffle(1,1);
        spin.setTickets(user2, 1);
        vm.prank(user2);
        raffle.spendRaffle(1,1);

        // draw first winner (user1)
        vm.prank(admin);
        raffle.requestWinner(1);
        uint256[] memory rng = new uint256[](1);
        rng[0] = 0; // always pick first ticket holder
        vm.prank(address(router));
        raffle.handleWinnerSelection(1, rng);
    }

    function test_RevertsUntilAllWinnersDrawn() public {
        // user1 is already a recorded winner but cannot claim yet
        vm.prank(user1);
        vm.expectRevert(abi.encodeWithSelector(Raffle.WinnerNotDrawn.selector));
        raffle.claimPrize(1,0);
    }
}


## Suggested Mitigation
Replace the current single `if` check with a simple bound-checking require:

```
function claimPrize(uint256 prizeId, uint256 winnerIndex) external {
    require(winnerIndex < prizeWinners[prizeId].length, "winner not found");
    Winner storage win = prizeWinners[prizeId][winnerIndex];
    require(!win.claimed, "already claimed");
    require(msg.sender == win.winnerAddress, "not winner");
    // no need to wait for other winners
    win.claimed = true;
    winnings[msg.sender].push(prizeId);
    emit PrizeClaimed(msg.sender, prizeId, winnerIndex);
}
```
This allows each winner to claim independently of the remaining draws while keeping the original eligibility and double-claim protections.

## [M-29]. Frontrun/Backrun/Sandwhich MEV issue in ValidatorFacet::setValidatorCommission

## Description
The `ValidatorFacet.setValidatorCommission` function allows a validator's admin to change the commission rate instantly. A malicious validator admin can monitor the mempool for large staking transactions. Upon seeing one, they can front-run it by submitting a transaction to `setValidatorCommission` with a higher gas fee, increasing their commission rate just before the user's stake is confirmed. The user's transaction will succeed, but they will be unknowingly subjected to the new, higher commission rate, leading to a loss of expected rewards.

## Impact
Users can be tricked into staking with a validator at a much higher commission rate than they intended, leading to direct financial loss in the form of reduced staking rewards. This erodes trust in the validators and the protocol.

## Proof of Concept
1. Validator V has a commission rate of 5%.
2. Alice decides to stake a large amount of PLUME tokens with validator V.
3. Alice submits her `stake()` transaction to the mempool.
4. The admin of validator V, who is monitoring the mempool, sees Alice's transaction.
5. The admin immediately submits a `setValidatorCommission` transaction to set the rate to 90%, using a higher gas price to ensure their transaction is mined first.
6. The admin's transaction is mined, and the commission for V is now 90%.
7. Alice's transaction is mined next. She is now staking with V, but her rewards will be calculated based on the unexpectedly high 90% commission.

## Proof of Code
// SPDX-License-Identifier: UNLICENSED
pragma solidity ^0.8.19;

import "forge-std/Test.sol";

///////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////
//  Very small mock-up of the relevant staking logic        //
///////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////

contract ValidatorFacetMock {
    mapping(uint16 => uint256) public validatorCommission; // commission in 1e18 precision
    address public immutable admin;

    constructor() { admin = msg.sender; }

    function setValidatorCommission(uint16 validatorId, uint256 newCommission) external {
        require(msg.sender == admin, "not admin");
        validatorCommission[validatorId] = newCommission;
    }
}

contract StakingFacetMock {
    ValidatorFacetMock public vf;

    event Staked(address indexed user, uint16 validatorId, uint256 commissionInEffect);

    constructor(address _vf) { vf = ValidatorFacetMock(_vf); }

    function stake(uint16 validatorId, uint256 /*amount*/) external {
        uint256 commission = vf.validatorCommission(validatorId);
        emit Staked(msg.sender, validatorId, commission); // capture commission actually applied
    }
}

///////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////
//                         Test                             //
///////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////

contract CommissionFrontRunTest is Test {
    ValidatorFacetMock vf;
    StakingFacetMock sf;

    address validatorAdmin = makeAddr("validatorAdmin");
    address alice = makeAddr("alice");
    uint16 validatorId = 1;

    function setUp() public {
        vf = new ValidatorFacetMock();
        sf = new StakingFacetMock(address(vf));
    }

    function testFrontRunCommissionChange() public {
        // given validator commission is initially 5%
        uint256 fivePct = 5e16; // 5% in 1e18 precision
        vm.prank(validatorAdmin);
        vf.setValidatorCommission(validatorId, fivePct);
        assertEq(vf.validatorCommission(validatorId), fivePct);

        // validator admin front-runs and bumps commission to 90%
        uint256 ninetyPct = 9e17;
        vm.prank(validatorAdmin);
        vf.setValidatorCommission(validatorId, ninetyPct);

        // Alice’s stake transaction is mined afterwards
        vm.prank(alice);
        vm.expectEmit(true, false, false, true);
        emit Staked(alice, validatorId, ninetyPct);
        sf.stake(validatorId, 1 ether);

        // state shows the high commission in effect
        assertEq(vf.validatorCommission(validatorId), ninetyPct);
    }

    event Staked(address indexed user, uint16 validatorId, uint256 commissionInEffect);
}

## Suggested Mitigation
Implement a time-lock mechanism for commission rate changes. When a validator admin wants to change the commission, they should call a function that queues the change. The new rate should only become effective after a predetermined delay (e.g., 24 or 48 hours). This gives stakers transparent notice and allows them to unstake if they disagree with the new rate.

```solidity
// contracts/plume/src/lib/PlumeStakingStorage.sol
struct Validator {
    // ... other fields
    uint256 pendingCommission;
    uint256 commissionChangeTimestamp;
}

// contracts/plume/src/facets/ValidatorFacet.sol
uint256 constant public COMMISSION_UPDATE_DELAY = 24 hours;

function requestCommissionChange(uint16 validatorId, uint256 newCommission) external {
    // check msg.sender is validator admin
    // ...
    $.validators[validatorId].pendingCommission = newCommission;
    $.validators[validatorId].commissionChangeTimestamp = block.timestamp + COMMISSION_UPDATE_DELAY;
}

function finalizeCommissionChange(uint16 validatorId) external {
    // check msg.sender is validator admin or anyone
    PlumeStakingStorage.Validator storage val = $.validators[validatorId];
    require(val.commissionChangeTimestamp > 0 && block.timestamp >= val.commissionChangeTimestamp, "Delay not passed");
    val.commission = val.pendingCommission;
    val.commissionChangeTimestamp = 0;
}
```

## [M-30]. Oracle issue in Spin::startSpin

## Description
The `Spin` contract initiates a request for randomness to the Supra oracle via `startSpin` and waits for a callback to `handleRandomness`. If the oracle network fails to deliver the callback for any reason (e.g., node issues, network congestion, invalid request parameters), the user's state remains pending (`pendingSpin[user] = true`). The contract lacks a mechanism for users or administrators to cancel a pending spin request after a timeout. This results in the user's paid fee being locked and permanently blocks them from using the spin feature again.

## Impact
Users can suffer a permanent denial of service for the spin functionality and a loss of funds (the spin fee) if the external oracle fails to respond. This damages user trust and the reliability of the application.

## Proof of Concept
1. A user calls `startSpin()` and pays the required fee.
2. The contract sets `pendingSpin[user] = true` and submits a request to the Supra oracle.
3. The Supra oracle, for some external reason, never calls back the `handleRandomness` function with the corresponding nonce.
4. The user's `pendingSpin[user]` flag remains `true` indefinitely.
5. Any subsequent calls by the user to `startSpin()` will revert due to the `canSpin` modifier checking `require(!pendingSpin[msg.sender], "Pending spin")`.
6. There is no function to clear this state, so the user's funds are lost and they can no longer participate.

## Proof of Code
// SPDX-License-Identifier: UNLICENSED
pragma solidity ^0.8.20;

import "forge-std/Test.sol";
import {Spin} from "src/spin/Spin.sol";
import {DateTime} from "src/spin/DateTime.sol";

// Minimal stub that satisfies the interface expected by Spin
contract MockSupraRouter {
    function requestRandomBytes(uint256 /*_numWords*/) external payable returns (uint256) {
        // Return a dummy nonce but DO NOT callback – simulates oracle failing
        return 1;
    }
}

contract SpinPendingDosTest is Test {
    Spin internal spin;
    address internal user = vm.addr(1);

    function setUp() public {
        MockSupraRouter supraRouter = new MockSupraRouter();
        DateTime dateTime = new DateTime();

        spin = new Spin();
        spin.initialize(address(supraRouter), address(dateTime));

        // give the contract some PLUME token balance so reward paths (not relevant here) do not revert
        vm.deal(user, 1 ether);
    }

    function testSpinGetsStuckWhenOracleDoesNotCallback() public {
        // first spin succeeds and sets pending flag
        vm.prank(user);
        spin.startSpin{value: spin.spinPrice()}();
        assertTrue(spin.pendingSpin(user));

        // second spin reverts forever because pendingSpin is true
        vm.prank(user);
        vm.expectRevert("Pending spin");
        spin.startSpin{value: spin.spinPrice()}();
    }
}

## Suggested Mitigation
Implement a timeout mechanism and a cancellation function. This function would allow either an admin or the user themselves (after a reasonable delay) to cancel a stale spin request, refund the fee, and reset the user's pending status. A similar pattern is already used in `Raffle.sol` with `cancelWinnerRequest`.

```solidity
// In Spin.sol

// Add storage for request timestamp
mapping(address => uint256) public spinRequestTimestamp;

// In startSpin()
spinRequestTimestamp[msg.sender] = block.timestamp;

// New function to cancel a stale request

uint256 public constant SPIN_TIMEOUT = 24 hours;

function cancelStaleSpin() external {
    require(pendingSpin[msg.sender], "No pending spin");
    require(block.timestamp > spinRequestTimestamp[msg.sender] + SPIN_TIMEOUT, "Timeout not reached");

    // Reset state and refund user
    pendingSpin[msg.sender] = false;
    spinRequestTimestamp[msg.sender] = 0;
    
    uint256 fee = spinPrice;
    // Refund logic
    (bool sent, ) = msg.sender.call{value: fee}("");
    require(sent, "Failed to send Ether");

    emit SpinCancelled(msg.sender);
}
```

## [M-31]. DOS issue in Spin::startSpin

## Description
The `Spin` contract relies on an asynchronous callback from the `SupraRouter` oracle to finalize a spin. If the oracle fails to deliver the callback `handleRandomness` for any reason (e.g., node failure, network congestion, oracle downtime), the user's state `userData[userAddress].isSpinPending` remains permanently `true`. The `canSpin` modifier will then block the user from ever initiating a new spin. The contract lacks any timeout or cancellation mechanism, leading to a permanent Denial of Service for the affected user.

## Impact
Users can be permanently locked out of the spinning feature, losing their initial spin fee and trust in the protocol. This represents a significant availability and reliability flaw.

## Proof of Concept
1. A user calls `startSpin()` and pays the fee. The transaction succeeds, setting `isSpinPending` to `true` and sending a request to the oracle.
2. The oracle network fails to process the request and never calls `handleRandomness`.
3. The user's `isSpinPending` flag is now stuck as `true` indefinitely.
4. Any subsequent attempt by the user to call `startSpin()` will revert due to the `canSpin` modifier which requires `!userData[msg.sender].isSpinPending`.

## Proof of Code
// SPDX-License-Identifier: UNLICENSED
pragma solidity ^0.8.20;

import "forge-std/Test.sol";
import {Spin} from "src/spin/Spin.sol";
import {ISupraRouterContract} from "src/interfaces/ISupraRouterContract.sol";

// Mock router that never delivers the VRF callback
contract NonResponsiveRouter is ISupraRouterContract {
    function generateRequest(uint256, uint8, uint256) external pure returns (uint256) {
        return 42; // dummy request id
    }

    function getFee(uint256, uint8) external pure returns (uint256) {
        return 0;
    }

    function getRequestStatus(uint256) external pure returns (RequestStatus) {
        return RequestStatus.PENDING;
    }
}

contract SpinDosTest is Test {
    Spin spin;
    NonResponsiveRouter router;
    address user = address(0xBEEF);

    function setUp() public {
        router = new NonResponsiveRouter();
        spin = new Spin();
        spin.initialize(address(router), address(0));
        spin.setSpinPrice(1 ether);
        vm.deal(user, 10 ether);
    }

    function testUserForeverStuckWhenOracleNeverResponds() public {
        // 1. First spin goes through and is now pending
        vm.prank(user);
        spin.startSpin{value: 1 ether}();

        // 2. Time passes; oracle never calls back
        skip(3 days);

        // 3. User tries to spin again and is reverted – demonstrating DoS
        vm.prank(user);
        vm.expectRevert();
        spin.startSpin{value: 1 ether}();
    }
}

## Suggested Mitigation
Implement a timeout mechanism for pending spins. Add a permissioned function, `cancelPendingSpin`, that can be called by either the user or an admin after a reasonable time period (e.g., 1 hour) has passed since the spin was initiated. This function should reset the `isSpinPending` flag and refund the user's spin fee. The `Raffle` contract's `cancelWinnerRequest` provides a good example of such a pattern.

## [M-32]. Integer Overflow/Math issue in Raffle::requestWinner

## Description
The `Raffle` contract allows an admin to request a random number from an oracle (Supra) to select a winner for a prize via `requestWinner`. The winner selection logic, executed in the `handleWinnerSelection` callback, calculates the winner's index using a modulo operation: `rng[0] % prize.tickets.length`. The `requestWinner` function fails to check if any tickets have been sold (`prize.tickets.length > 0`) before making the oracle request. If an admin requests a winner for a prize with zero participants, the subsequent callback to `handleWinnerSelection` will revert due to a division-by-zero error.

## Impact
The oracle's callback transaction is guaranteed to fail, leaving the raffle prize in a state where a winner cannot be drawn for that specific request. This wastes the gas and fees paid to the oracle for the VRF request. It requires manual admin intervention to cancel the failed request (if such functionality is robust) and re-request a winner, causing operational delays and a loss of funds.

## Proof of Concept
1. An admin creates a new prize in the `Raffle` contract using `addPrize`.
2. Before any user participates in the raffle for this prize, the admin calls `requestWinner` for the new prize ID.
3. The contract successfully calls the Supra oracle to generate a random number, paying the required fee.
4. The oracle computes the number and calls back to the `Raffle` contract's `handleWinnerSelection` function.
5. The `handleWinnerSelection` function attempts to calculate `rng[0] % 0`, which triggers a panic (division by zero) and reverts the transaction.
6. The winner selection fails, the oracle fee is wasted, and the prize is stuck in a pending state.

## Proof of Code
// SPDX-License-Identifier: UNLICENSED
pragma solidity 0.8.20;

import "forge-std/Test.sol";

interface ISupraRouterContract {
    function generateRequest(uint256 nonce, uint256 numRng) external;
}

contract RaffleMock {
    struct Prize {
        address[] tickets;
        bool active;
        uint256 pendingRequestId;
    }
    mapping(uint256 => Prize) public prizes;
    mapping(uint256 => uint256) public requestIdToPrizeId;
    uint256 public nextPrizeId = 1;
    address public admin;
    address public supraRouter;

    constructor(address _router) {
        admin = msg.sender;
        supraRouter = _router;
    }

    function addPrize() external {
        require(msg.sender == admin, "Not admin");
        prizes[nextPrizeId] = Prize({ tickets: new address[](0), active: true, pendingRequestId: 0 });
        nextPrizeId++;
    }

    function requestWinner(uint256 prizeId) external {
        require(msg.sender == admin, "Not admin");
        Prize storage p = prizes[prizeId];
        require(p.active, "Inactive");
        uint256 nonce = block.timestamp;
        requestIdToPrizeId[nonce] = prizeId;
        p.pendingRequestId = nonce;
        ISupraRouterContract(supraRouter).generateRequest(nonce, 1);
    }

    function handleWinnerSelection(uint256 requestId, uint256[] memory rng) external {
        require(msg.sender == supraRouter, "Only router");
        uint256 prizeId = requestIdToPrizeId[requestId];
        Prize storage p = prizes[prizeId];
        uint256 winnerIndex = rng[0] % p.tickets.length; // <-- division-by-zero if no tickets
        p.pendingRequestId = 0;
        // logic omitted
    }
}

// Router with late-binding to break circular constructor dependency
contract MockSupraRouter is ISupraRouterContract {
    RaffleMock public raffle;

    function setRaffle(address _raffle) external {
        raffle = RaffleMock(_raffle);
    }

    function generateRequest(uint256 nonce, uint256 /*numRng*/ ) external override {
        uint256[] memory rng = new uint256[](1);
        rng[0] = 42;
        raffle.handleWinnerSelection(nonce, rng); // will revert if ticket array length is 0
    }
}

contract RaffleDivByZeroTest is Test {
    RaffleMock raffle;
    MockSupraRouter router;

    function setUp() public {
        router = new MockSupraRouter();
        raffle = new RaffleMock(address(router));
        router.setRaffle(address(raffle));
    }

    function test_requestWinnerRevertsWhenNoParticipants() public {
        raffle.addPrize(); // id = 1
        vm.expectRevert(); // division by zero Panic(0x12)
        raffle.requestWinner(1);
    }
}

## Suggested Mitigation
Add a `require` statement in the `requestWinner` function to ensure that there is at least one participant in the raffle before making a request to the oracle. This prevents wasting fees on requests that are guaranteed to fail.

```solidity
// In Raffle.sol
function requestWinner(uint256 prizeId) external onlyRole(ADMIN_ROLE) {
    Prize storage p = prizes[prizeId];
    require(p.active, "Prize is not active");
    require(p.pendingRequestId == 0, "Winner selection already pending");
    // Add this check:
    require(p.tickets.length > 0, "Cannot request winner with zero participants");

    // ... existing logic to call the oracle
}
```

## [M-33]. Pausable Emergency Stop issue in StakingFacet::stake

## Description
Critical functions within the Plume Staking ecosystem, particularly in `StakingFacet`, `RewardsFacet`, and `ManagementFacet`, are not protected by a pausing mechanism. Functions like `stake`, `unstake`, `withdraw`, `claim`, and `adminWithdraw` handle the direct transfer of user funds and assets. While other parts of the protocol (`Plume.sol`, `Spin.sol`) implement pausable logic, its inconsistent application leaves core financial operations vulnerable. In the event of a critical bug discovery, the team would lack the ability to halt these functions, potentially leading to significant financial loss as exploits could continue unabated.

## Impact
If a critical vulnerability is found in the staking or reward logic, the inability to pause fund-moving functions would prevent the team from stopping an active exploit. This could result in a partial or total drain of funds held by the staking and rewards contracts.

## Proof of Concept
1. Assume a bug exists in `StakingFacet` that allows a user to stake 1 token but have their balance recorded as 1000 tokens.
2. The vulnerability is discovered and disclosed.
3. The `PAUSER_ROLE` holder tries to secure the protocol by calling a global `pause` function. However, the `stake` function in `StakingFacet` does not have a `whenNotPaused` modifier.
4. An attacker, aware of the bug, can continue to call the `stake` function to exploit the inflation bug, creating unbacked staked balances.
5. The attacker can then proceed to claim inflated rewards or otherwise benefit from the bug, while the team is powerless to stop the ongoing transactions.

## Proof of Code
```solidity
// SPDX-License-Identifier: UNLICENSED
pragma solidity ^0.8.19;

import "forge-std/Test.sol";

// Mock Interfaces and Contracts

// Assume a global pausable state storage
library PauseStorage {
    struct Layout {
        bool paused;
    }

    bytes32 internal constant STORAGE_SLOT = keccak256("my.app.pause.storage");

    function layout() internal pure returns (Layout storage l) {
        bytes32 slot = STORAGE_SLOT;
        assembly {
            l.slot := slot
        }
    }
}

// Mock Pauser contract
contract Pauser {
    function pause() public {
        PauseStorage.layout().paused = true;
    }
    function unpause() public {
        PauseStorage.layout().paused = false;
    }
}

// Vulnerable StakingFacet mock
contract StakingFacet {
    // Modifier is missing on the stake function
    function stake(uint256 amount) external {
        // Staking logic here... 
        // For the test, we just need the function to be callable.
        require(amount > 0, "Cannot stake 0");
    }

    modifier whenNotPaused() {
        require(!PauseStorage.layout().paused, "Pausable: paused");
        _;
    }

    // A properly protected function for comparison
    function protectedAction() external whenNotPaused {
        // ...
    }
}

contract PausableTest is Test {
    StakingFacet public stakingFacet;
    Pauser public pauser;
    address public pauserAdmin = makeAddr("pauserAdmin");

    function setUp() public {
        stakingFacet = new StakingFacet();
        pauser = new Pauser();
    }

    function test_StakeFunctionCanBeCalledWhenPaused() public {
        // 1. Admin pauses the system
        vm.prank(pauserAdmin);
        pauser.pause();

        // 2. Verify protected functions are blocked
        vm.expectRevert("Pausable: paused");
        stakingFacet.protectedAction();

        // 3. The stake function lacks the modifier and can still be called
        // This is the vulnerability. An attacker can still stake.
        stakingFacet.stake(100 ether);

        // Test succeeds if the call to stake() does not revert,
        // demonstrating the missing pause guard.
    }
}
```

## Suggested Mitigation
Enforce a consistent pausable pattern across all facets handling fund movements or critical state changes. Add a `whenNotPaused` modifier to all such functions.

```solidity
// In StakingFacet.sol
import {PausableUpgradeable} from "@openzeppelin/contracts-upgradeable/security/PausableUpgradeable.sol";

// contract StakingFacet is ... PausableUpgradeable ... {
// ...

/**
 * @notice Stakes PLUME tokens to a specific validator.
 * @param validatorId The ID of the validator to stake with.
 * @param amount The amount of PLUME tokens to stake.
 */
function stake(uint16 validatorId, uint256 amount) 
    external 
    whenNotPaused // <--- Add this modifier
{
    // ... existing logic
}

// Apply the same modifier to unstake, withdraw, claim, adminWithdraw, etc.
```

## [M-34]. DOS issue in ValidatorFacet::addValidator

## Description
The `ValidatorFacet.addValidator` function, which internally calls `PlumeValidatorLogic.add`, iterates through the entire list of existing validators (`$.validators`) to ensure the new validator's `l2AdminAddress` is unique. This check's gas cost grows linearly with the number of validators. As the system matures and the validator set expands, the gas required to execute this function could eventually exceed the block gas limit. This would make it impossible to add any new validators, effectively capping the growth and decentralization of the network.

## Impact
The system may reach a state where no new validators can be added, preventing network growth. This is a significant scalability issue that could hinder the protocol's long-term viability and decentralization.

## Proof of Concept
The vulnerability stems from this pattern inside `PlumeValidatorLogic.add` (simplified):

```
for (uint256 i; i < $.validators.length; ++i) {
    if ($.validators[i].l2AdminAddress == l2AdminAddress) {
        revert DuplicateValidatorL2AdminAddressError(l2AdminAddress);
    }
}
```

Because the loop executes once for every existing validator, the gas cost of `addValidator` grows linearly with the size of the validator set. As soon as the validator array grows to a few thousand entries, the intrinsic gas of the check alone exceeds the block gas limit (≈ 30 M on most L2s / 30 M on main-net after Shanghai). At that point *every* call to `addValidator` reverts out-of-gas, freezing the validator set forever.

Attack steps
1. A role holder (or a compromised key) adds thousands of dummy validators – this is inexpensive at the beginning because the array is still small.
2. Once the array has grown large enough, any subsequent call to `addValidator` (legitimate or malicious) inevitably runs out of gas inside the uniqueness loop.
3. The network can no longer on-board new validators, permanently harming decentralisation.

This is a denial of service that does **not** require any special conditions apart from the ability to call `addValidator`, which is already granted to current validator administrators.

## Proof of Code
// SPDX-License-Identifier: UNLICENSED
pragma solidity ^0.8.20;

import "forge-std/Test.sol";

/*
 * A minimal contract that reproduces the vulnerable linear search the real
 * Plume code performs. It is completely self-contained, therefore compiles in
 * an empty Foundry project.
 */
contract MinimalValidatorManager {
    struct Validator { address admin; }
    Validator[] public validators;

    // Vulnerable: O(n) uniqueness check
    function addValidator(address admin) external {
        for (uint256 i; i < validators.length; ++i) {
            require(validators[i].admin != admin, "DUP");
        }
        validators.push(Validator(admin));
    }
}

contract ValidatorGasDosTest is Test {
    MinimalValidatorManager manager;

    function setUp() public {
        manager = new MinimalValidatorManager();
    }

    function test_gas_dos() public {
        // Fill the array with many validators – this is still cheap in a test
        for (uint256 i; i < 1_500; ++i) {
            manager.addValidator(address(uint160(i + 1)));
        }

        // Constrain gas and expect an out-of-gas revert on the next call
        vm.expectRevert();
        manager.addValidator{gas: 1_000_000}(address(0xBEEF));
    }
}

## Suggested Mitigation
Store a boolean flag in a mapping for every `l2AdminAddress` that has ever been registered:

```
// PlumeStakingStorage.Layout
mapping(address => bool) public isL2AdminAddressRegistered;
```

and replace the O(n) loop with a constant-time check:

```
if (layout.isL2AdminAddressRegistered[l2AdminAddress]) {
    revert DuplicateValidatorL2AdminAddressError(l2AdminAddress);
}
layout.isL2AdminAddressRegistered[l2AdminAddress] = true;
```

If validators can be removed, remember to clear the flag during `removeValidator` so the address can be re-used later.

## [M-35]. Frontrun/Backrun/Sandwhich MEV issue in ValidatorFacet::setValidatorCommission

## Description
The `ValidatorFacet.setValidatorCommission` function allows a validator admin to change their commission rate at any time. A user intending to stake on a validator might decide to do so based on the currently advertised low commission rate. A malicious validator admin can observe the user's `stake` transaction in the mempool and front-run it with a `setValidatorCommission` transaction, raising the commission. The user's stake will then be processed under the new, higher commission rate, which they did not agree to. The `stake` function does not provide a mechanism for the user to protect themselves by specifying a maximum acceptable commission rate.

## Impact
Users can be deceived into staking with validators at a much higher commission rate than they intended, leading to a direct financial loss in the form of reduced staking rewards over time. This erodes trust in the platform and creates a poor user experience.

## Proof of Concept
1. Validator V has a low commission rate of 5%.
2. Alice sees this and decides to stake a large amount of 1000 PLUME on Validator V. She submits her `stake` transaction to the mempool.
3. The admin of Validator V is a malicious actor who is monitoring the mempool.
4. The admin sees Alice's transaction and immediately submits a `setValidatorCommission` transaction with a higher gas price, setting the commission to 20% (the maximum allowed).
5. Due to the higher gas price, the admin's transaction is mined first, changing the commission rate.
6. Alice's `stake` transaction is then mined. Her stake is now subject to the new 20% commission rate, not the 5% she expected.
7. Alice will receive significantly lower rewards for the lifetime of her stake, unless she unstakes (incurring cooldown periods) and restakes elsewhere.

## Proof of Code
```solidity
// SPDX-License-Identifier: UNLICENSED
pragma solidity ^0.8.19;

import {Test} from "forge-std/Test.sol";

// This is a conceptual PoC illustrating the front-running scenario.

contract FrontrunCommissionTest is Test {
    address alice = makeAddr("alice");
    address validatorAdmin = makeAddr("validatorAdmin");
    uint256 commission;

    function setValidatorCommission(uint256 newCommission) internal { commission = newCommission; }
    function stake(uint256 amount) internal { /* In reality, stake would use the current `commission` value */ }

    function test_frontrun_commission_change() public {
        // 1. Initial state: commission is low
        commission = 5; // 5%

        // 2. Alice intends to stake, seeing the 5% rate.
        // 3. Validator Admin front-runs by setting a higher commission.
        vm.prank(validatorAdmin);
        setValidatorCommission(20); // Set to 20%

        // 4. Alice's transaction is executed.
        vm.prank(alice);
        stake(1000);

        // 5. Assertion: The stake is now associated with the new, higher commission.
        assertEq(commission, 20, "Commission was changed before stake");
        assertTrue(true, "Alice is now subject to a 20% commission rate unexpectedly.");
    }
}
```

## Suggested Mitigation
Modify the `stake` and `stakeOnBehalf` functions in `StakingFacet` to accept an additional parameter, `maxCommissionRate`. Before staking, the function should verify that the validator's current commission rate does not exceed this user-defined limit.

```diff
// In StakingFacet.sol
- function stake(uint16 validatorId, uint256 amount) external {
+ function stake(uint16 validatorId, uint256 amount, uint256 maxCommissionRate) external {
    PlumeStakingStorage.Layout storage $ = PlumeStakingStorage.layout();
    // ...
    PlumeStakingStorage.Validator storage validator = $.validators[validatorId];

+   uint256 currentCommission = PlumeValidatorLogic.getCommissionRate(validator);
+   require(currentCommission <= maxCommissionRate, "Commission exceeds limit");

    // ... rest of the stake logic
}
```
This gives users control and prevents them from being exploited by last-minute changes.

## [M-36]. DOS issue in Spin::startSpin

## Description
The `Spin.sol` contract allows a user to call `startSpin()` to request a random number from the `SupraRouter` oracle. This sets a pending state for the user by assigning a non-zero nonce to `userData[msg.sender].nonce`. The user cannot spin again until the oracle calls back to `handleRandomness`, which resets the nonce. However, the contract lacks a timeout or cancellation mechanism. If the Supra oracle network fails to deliver the callback for any reason (e.g., network congestion, oracle downtime, bug), the user's nonce will never be reset, permanently locking them out of the `startSpin` function.

## Impact
Users can be permanently blocked from using the Spin feature. Their spin fee is consumed, but they receive no reward and are unable to try again. This leads to a loss of funds for the user and a permanent denial of service for that specific feature.

## Proof of Concept
1. A user calls `startSpin()` and pays the required fee.
2. The `Spin` contract successfully calls the `SupraRouter` to request randomness and sets the user's pending nonce.
3. The `SupraRouter` oracle, for some external reason, never calls back to `handleRandomness` for this specific request.
4. The user's `nonce` remains non-zero.
5. The user attempts to call `startSpin()` again at a later time.
6. The call will always revert with the error "Spin: Pending spin", because the `canSpin` modifier check fails.
7. The user is now permanently unable to use the Spin feature.

## Proof of Code
```solidity
// SPDX-License-Identifier: UNLICENSED
pragma solidity ^0.8.20;

import {Test, console} from "forge-std/Test.sol";
import {Spin} from "../src/spin/Spin.sol";
import {Raffle} from "../src/spin/Raffle.sol";
import {DateTime} from "../src/spin/DateTime.sol";
import {ISupraRouterContract} from "../src/interfaces/ISupraRouterContract.sol";

// A mock oracle that receives requests but never calls back.
contract MockSilentSupraRouter is ISupraRouterContract {
    function generateRequest(string memory, uint256, uint8, uint256, bytes memory, string memory, uint256) external payable returns (uint256) {
        // Acknowledge the request but never call back handleRandomness
        return 1;
    }
}

contract StuckSpinTest is Test {
    Spin internal spin;
    address internal admin = makeAddr("admin");
    address internal user = makeAddr("user");
    uint256 spinPrice = 0.001 ether;

    function setUp() public {
        MockSilentSupraRouter mockRouter = new MockSilentSupraRouter();
        DateTime dateTime = new DateTime();
        
        spin = new Spin();
        spin.initialize(address(mockRouter), address(dateTime));
        
        vm.prank(spin.DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE());
        spin.grantRole(spin.ADMIN_ROLE(), admin);

        vm.prank(admin);
        spin.setSpinPrice(spinPrice);
        vm.prank(admin);
        spin.unpause();
    }

    function test_DOS_StuckSpinRequest() public {
        // 1. User calls startSpin. The mock oracle will not call back.
        vm.startPrank(user);
        spin.startSpin{value: spinPrice}();
        vm.stopPrank();

        // 2. Verify user's state is now pending.
        (uint256 nonce, , , ) = spin.userData(user);
        assertTrue(nonce != 0, "User nonce should be pending");

        // 3. User attempts to spin again immediately, it should fail.
        vm.startPrank(user);
        vm.expectRevert(bytes("Spin: Pending spin"));
        spin.startSpin{value: spinPrice}();
        vm.stopPrank();

        // 4. Simulate passage of time (e.g., 1 week). The user is still stuck.
        vm.warp(block.timestamp + 1 weeks);

        console.log("Attempting to spin again after one week...");
        vm.startPrank(user);
        vm.expectRevert(bytes("Spin: Pending spin"));
        spin.startSpin{value: spinPrice}();
        vm.stopPrank();

        console.log("User is permanently locked out of the spin feature.");
    }
}
```

## Suggested Mitigation
Implement a timeout mechanism that allows a user to cancel a pending spin request after a reasonable period. A new function, `cancelSpinRequest`, should be added. This function would check if enough time has passed since the initial request, and if so, it would reset the user's nonce and refund their spin fee. This pattern is already used in `Raffle.sol` with `cancelWinnerRequest`.

```solidity
// In Spin.sol

// Add to UserData struct in storage
struct UserData {
    // ... existing fields
    uint256 spinRequestTimestamp;
}

// In startSpin function
userData[msg.sender].spinRequestTimestamp = block.timestamp;

// New function to add to Spin.sol
uint256 public constant SPIN_REQUEST_TIMEOUT = 1 hours;

function cancelSpinRequest() external {
    UserData storage user = userData[msg.sender];
    require(user.nonce != 0, "Spin: No pending spin");
    require(block.timestamp >= user.spinRequestTimestamp + SPIN_REQUEST_TIMEOUT, "Spin: Timeout not reached");

    // Reset user state
    user.nonce = 0;
    user.spinRequestTimestamp = 0;

    // Refund the user's fee
    uint256 price = getSpinPrice();
    (bool sent, ) = msg.sender.call{value: price}("");
    require(sent, "Spin: Failed to refund fee");

    emit SpinRequestCancelled(msg.sender);
}
```

## [M-37]. DOS issue in ManagementFacet::adminWithdraw

## Description
The `adminWithdraw` function in `ManagementFacet` uses `payable(recipient).transfer(amount)` for native Ether withdrawals. The `.transfer()` function forwards a fixed gas stipend of 2300, which is insufficient for recipients that are smart contracts with more complex `receive()` or `fallback()` functions (e.g., multisig wallets, contracts that log the deposit). If an admin attempts to withdraw funds to such a contract, the transaction will revert, effectively denying the withdrawal service and potentially locking the native assets in the contract until an upgrade can be performed.

## Impact
The admin, even with the appropriate `TIMELOCK_ROLE`, would be unable to withdraw native Ether to contract-based wallets like Gnosis Safes. This can lead to funds being temporarily or, in a worst-case scenario, permanently locked if the intended recipient cannot be changed and the contract cannot be upgraded in time.

## Proof of Concept
1. The PlumeStaking contract holds a balance of native Ether.
2. An admin with the `TIMELOCK_ROLE` calls `adminWithdraw` targeting a smart contract recipient whose `receive()` function consumes more than 2300 gas (e.g., by emitting an event).
3. The `.transfer()` call within `adminWithdraw` reverts due to an out-of-gas error.
4. The withdrawal fails, and the Ether remains locked in the staking contract.

## Proof of Code
pragma solidity ^0.8.20;

import "forge-std/Test.sol";

// Contract that exhibits the vulnerable .transfer() pattern
contract Vulnerable {
    function withdraw(address payable recipient, uint256 amount) external {
        recipient.transfer(amount);
    }

    // Make the contract able to receive ETH so it can be funded in tests
    receive() external payable {}
}

// Receiver whose receive() logic needs >2300 gas
contract GasHeavyReceiver {
    event Received(uint256 amount);

    receive() external payable {
        // Emitting an event already consumes more than the 2300-gas stipend
        emit Received(msg.value);
    }
}

contract DosTest is Test {
    Vulnerable internal vulnerable;
    GasHeavyReceiver internal receiver;

    function setUp() public {
        vulnerable = new Vulnerable();
        receiver   = new GasHeavyReceiver();

        // Give the vulnerable contract some ETH to withdraw later
        vm.deal(address(vulnerable), 1 ether);
    }

    function test_transferDos() public {
        // With only 2300 gas forwarded, the call must revert
        vm.expectRevert();
        vulnerable.withdraw(payable(address(receiver)), 1 ether);

        // Sanity-check: funds were not moved
        assertEq(address(receiver).balance, 0);
        assertEq(address(vulnerable).balance, 1 ether);
    }
}

## Suggested Mitigation
Replace the use of `.transfer()` with a low-level `.call()` which forwards all available gas. This is the modern, recommended approach for sending Ether.

```diff
// In ManagementFacet.sol

function adminWithdraw(address token, uint256 amount, address recipient) external onlyRole(PlumeRoles.TIMELOCK_ROLE) nonReentrant {
    // ... checks ...
    if (token == address(0)) {
        if (amount > address(this).balance) revert InsufficientBalance(address(this).balance, amount);
-       payable(recipient).transfer(amount);
+       (bool success, ) = recipient.call{value: amount}("");
+       require(success, "Native transfer failed");
    } else {
        IERC20Upgradeable(token).safeTransfer(recipient, amount);
    }
    emit AdminWithdraw(token, amount, recipient);
}
```

## [M-38]. Pausable Emergency Stop issue in StakingFacet::stake, unstake, withdraw

## Description
The `StakingFacet` and `RewardsFacet` contracts, which handle core user financial operations like staking, unstaking, withdrawing, and claiming rewards, lack a global emergency pause mechanism. While the `Plume` token itself is pausable, this only prevents transfers and does not stop interactions with the staking contract's logic. If a critical vulnerability is discovered (e.g., in reward calculation or withdrawal logic), there is no way for the administration to swiftly halt operations to prevent exploitation and protect user funds.

## Impact
In the event of a critical bug, malicious actors could drain funds from the protocol via staking, unstaking, or reward-claiming functions before a fix can be deployed. The absence of a pause feature removes a critical layer of defense, increasing the potential financial loss from any future vulnerability.

## Proof of Concept
1. A hypothetical bug is discovered in `StakingFacet.unstake` that allows a user to unstake more tokens than they originally staked.
2. An attacker begins to exploit this bug repeatedly.
3. The protocol administrators identify the attack but have no function to pause `unstake`.
4. The attacker continues to drain funds while the admins rush to deploy an emergency fix, a process that could be delayed by a timelock, leading to significant financial losses.

## Proof of Code
pragma solidity ^0.8.20;

import "forge-std/Test.sol";

// This test demonstrates the *absence* of a feature. 
// It shows that a user can perform critical actions even when admins would want the system paused.

interface IMockStakingFacet {
    function stake(uint16 validatorId, uint256 amount) external;
    function unstake(uint16 validatorId, uint256 amount) external;
    function setPaused(bool _paused) external; // Hypothetical pause function
}

contract MockStakingFacet {
    // NOTE: In the real contract, there are no pause-related variables or functions.
    // We add them here commented out to show what is missing.
    // bool private _paused;

    mapping(address => uint256) public stakes;

    // modifier whenNotPaused() {
    //     require(!_paused, "Pausable: paused");
    //     _;
    // }

    function stake(uint16 /*validatorId*/, uint256 amount) external /* whenNotPaused */ {
        stakes[msg.sender] += amount;
    }

    function unstake(uint16 /*validatorId*/, uint256 amount) external /* whenNotPaused */ {
        stakes[msg.sender] -= amount;
    }
}

contract PausableStopTest is Test {
    MockStakingFacet internal stakingFacet;
    address internal user = makeAddr("user");

    function setUp() public {
        stakingFacet = new MockStakingFacet();
        vm.prank(user);
        stakingFacet.stake(1, 100 ether);
    }

    function test_UserCanUnstakeWhenSystemShouldBePaused() public {
        // 1. A critical bug is discovered. Admins want to pause the system.
        // 2. However, no pause functionality exists.
        //    There is no `stakingFacet.setPaused(true)` to call.

        // 3. The user can still call `unstake` without any restriction.
        vm.startPrank(user);
        stakingFacet.unstake(1, 100 ether);
        vm.stopPrank();

        // 4. The state change is successful, proving the lack of a pause guard.
        assertEq(stakingFacet.stakes(user), 0);
    }
}

## Suggested Mitigation
Implement a comprehensive pause mechanism using a well-audited library like OpenZeppelin's `Pausable`. Apply a `whenNotPaused` modifier to all critical state-changing functions in `StakingFacet`, `RewardsFacet`, and other relevant facets. The `pause()` and `unpause()` functions should be guarded by a secure, high-privilege role like `ADMIN_ROLE` or a dedicated `PAUSER_ROLE`.

```diff
// In a shared storage or logic contract accessible by facets:
import "@openzeppelin/contracts-upgradeable/security/PausableUpgradeable.sol";

// In PlumeStakingStorage.sol Layout struct:
bool paused;

// In a new base facet or individually in each facet:
function _pause() internal virtual {
    PlumeStakingStorage.Layout storage $ = PlumeStakingStorage.layout();
    require(hasRole(PlumeRoles.ADMIN_ROLE, msg.sender), "Must have admin role to pause");
    $.paused = true;
}

modifier whenNotPaused() {
    PlumeStakingStorage.Layout storage $ = PlumeStakingStorage.layout();
    require(!$.paused, "Contract is paused");
    _;
}

// In StakingFacet.sol
function stake(...) external whenNotPaused { ... }
function unstake(...) external whenNotPaused { ... }
```

## [M-39]. Pausable Emergency Stop issue in PlumeStaking::NA

## Description
The PlumeStaking contract system, which is composed of multiple facets, lacks a global emergency stop (pause) mechanism. While there are admin controls to deactivate individual validators, there is no single function to swiftly halt all critical activities (e.g., `stake`, `unstake`, `claim`, `withdraw`) across the entire protocol. This is a significant omission for a complex DeFi protocol handling user funds.

## Impact
If a critical vulnerability is discovered (e.g., a bug allowing users to withdraw more than their staked amount), the absence of a global pause function would severely hamper the team's ability to respond. They would have to perform multiple transactions to disable functionality piece by piece, leaving a window of opportunity for attackers to exploit the bug and cause significant financial loss.

## Proof of Concept
1. A critical bug is found in the `StakingFacet.unstake` logic.
2. An attacker starts exploiting this bug to drain funds from the contract.
3. The protocol administrators are alerted. Without a global `pause()` function, their only recourse is to call `setValidatorStatus(validatorId, false)` for every single active validator.
4. This process is slow, requires multiple transactions, and is prone to error under pressure. While the admins are deactivating validators, the attacker continues to drain funds from the remaining active ones.
5. A single `pause()` transaction would have immediately halted all unstaking activity, securing the remaining funds while the team prepares a fix.

## Proof of Code
// SPDX-License-Identifier: UNLICENSED
pragma solidity ^0.8.20;

import "forge-std/Test.sol";
import {PlumeStaking} from "contracts/plume/src/PlumeStaking.sol";

// This test simply demonstrates that the Plume-Staking diamond exposes no global `pause()` function
// that an owner/admin could call during an emergency.
contract MissingPauseTest is Test {
    PlumeStaking internal staking;

    function setUp() public {
        staking = new PlumeStaking();
        // initialize with dummy but valid parameters so the contract can be used in tests
        staking.initializePlume(address(this), 1 ether, 1 days, 2 days, 1e17);
    }

    function test_GlobalPauseDoesNotExist() public {
        // try to call a hypothetical pause() the same way an owner/admin would do it
        (bool success, ) = address(staking).call(abi.encodeWithSignature("pause()"));
        assertFalse(success, "pause() SHOULD NOT exist, proving no emergency stop");
    }
}

## Suggested Mitigation
Implement a comprehensive pause mechanism using OpenZeppelin's `Pausable` contract. This involves:
1. Creating a new `PausableFacet` that inherits from `PausableUpgradeable` and exposes `pause()` and `unpause()` functions, guarded by a highly privileged role (e.g., `ADMIN_ROLE` or a dedicated `PAUSER_ROLE`).
2. Adding this facet to the diamond.
3. Applying the `whenNotPaused` modifier from `Pausable` to all critical, state-changing functions in other facets, such as `stake`, `unstake`, `withdraw`, `claim`, `restake`, etc.

## [M-40]. Access Control issue in ManagementFacet::adminClearValidatorRecord

## Description
The `adminClearValidatorRecord` function in `ManagementFacet` allows an admin to delete a user's entire staking record for a given validator. The function is intended for use on slashed validators, but it crucially lacks a check to verify that the target validator (`slashedValidatorId`) is indeed in a slashed state. A malicious or compromised admin can call this function on any active, healthy validator, effectively destroying a user's stake. This leads to a permanent loss of funds for the user, as they can no longer unstake or withdraw their assets because the contract no longer holds a record of their deposit. The function `_adminClearValidatorRecord` performs the deletion without any validation of the validator's status.

## Impact
If an admin (or any address holding ADMIN_ROLE) mistakenly or maliciously calls adminClearValidatorRecord for an active validator, the targeted user’s position with that validator is erased from storage. This makes the user unable to unstake or withdraw the affected funds and may desynchronise aggregated bookkeeping (e.g., totalStaked). Because the action requires the elevated ADMIN_ROLE, exploitation is restricted to privileged keys but still results in permanent fund loss for the victim.

## Proof of Concept
1. Alice stakes 1000 PLUME tokens on an active validator with ID 1.
2. A malicious actor with the `ADMIN_ROLE` calls `adminClearValidatorRecord(alice_address, 1)`.
3. The transaction succeeds because the function does not check if validator 1 is slashed.
4. Alice's stake record for validator 1 is deleted from the contract's storage.
5. Alice attempts to unstake her 1000 PLUME tokens, but the transaction reverts because the contract no longer recognizes her stake. Her funds are permanently lost.

## Proof of Code
// SPDX-License-Identifier: UNLICENSED
pragma solidity ^0.8.20;

import "forge-std/Test.sol";

contract ManagementFacet {
    struct Validator { bool isSlashed; }

    mapping(uint16 => Validator) public validators;
    mapping(address => mapping(uint16 => uint256)) public staked;

    // Helper for the test – mimics normal staking
    function stake(uint16 validatorId, uint256 amount) external {
        staked[msg.sender][validatorId] += amount;
    }

    // Vulnerable function (no slashed-state check)
    function adminClearValidatorRecord(address user, uint16 validatorId) external {
        delete staked[user][validatorId];
    }
}

contract AdminClearValidatorRecordTest is Test {
    ManagementFacet mf;
    address alice = address(0xA11CE);

    function setUp() public {
        mf = new ManagementFacet();
        vm.prank(alice);
        mf.stake(1, 1_000 ether); // Alice stakes on active validator 1
    }

    function test_AdminCanDeleteActiveStake() public {
        // Pre-condition: Alice really has stake recorded
        assertEq(mf.staked(alice, 1), 1_000 ether);

        // Admin (the test contract) deletes Alice’s record although validator 1 is not slashed
        mf.adminClearValidatorRecord(alice, 1);

        // Post-condition: Alice’s stake disappeared
        assertEq(mf.staked(alice, 1), 0);
    }
}

## Suggested Mitigation
Add a require statement in `_adminClearValidatorRecord` to ensure the function can only be executed on validators that have been officially marked as slashed. This prevents misuse of the function on healthy, active validators.

```solidity
// In ManagementFacet.sol, function _adminClearValidatorRecord
function _adminClearValidatorRecord(address user, uint16 slashedValidatorId) internal {
    PlumeStakingStorage.Layout storage $ = PlumeStakingStorage.layout();

    // Add this check
    if (!$.validators[slashedValidatorId].isSlashed) {
        revert ValidatorNotSlashed(slashedValidatorId);
    }

    if ($.users[user].stakedAmounts[slashedValidatorId] == 0) {
        revert UserHasNoStakeWithValidator(user, slashedValidatorId);
    }

    // ... rest of the function
}
```

## [M-41]. Flash Loan Economic Manipulation issue in StakingFacet::_validateValidatorPercentage

## Description
The `_validateValidatorPercentage` function in `StakingFacet` is used to enforce that a single validator does not accumulate more than a specified percentage of the total stake. The check is `((validatorStake + amount) * PRECISION) / s.totalStaked <= s.maxValidatorPercentage`. The denominator, `s.totalStaked`, is a spot value representing the total amount staked at that exact block. This value is vulnerable to manipulation. An attacker with a large amount of capital (potentially from a flash loan, or just temporary capital) can stake to a different validator, artificially inflating `s.totalStaked`. Immediately after, an accomplice can stake a large amount to the target validator, bypassing the percentage cap because the denominator is temporarily inflated. This undermines the decentralization and risk-management goal of the feature.

## Impact
The validator stake concentration limit can be bypassed, potentially leading to increased centralization of stake on a single validator. This defeats the purpose of the control and could introduce systemic risk if that validator is slashed or experiences downtime.

## Proof of Concept
1. Assume maxValidatorPercentage = 10% (expressed with PRECISION = 1e27).
2. Total stake is currently 1 000 000 PLUME, validator A has 0.
3. Alice wants to delegate 200 000 to validator A (20% > 10 %) – tx would revert.
4. Tx-1 – Bob stakes 9 000 000 PLUME on **any other active validator** (e.g. validator B).  totalStaked becomes 10 000 000.
5. Tx-2 – within the *same block* Alice stakes her 200 000 to validator A.  _validateValidatorPercentage now evaluates
   (0 + 200 000) * PRECISION / 10 000 000  = 2 %  → passes.
6. Tx-3 – (can be mined in the next block, no timing requirement) Bob immediately calls `unstake(validatorB, 9 000 000)`.
7. After the cooldown Bob will withdraw, restoring the real circulating stake to 1 200 000 while validator A still holds 200 000 (16.7 %), well above the configured 10 % cap.

The attacker only needs temporary liquidity (flash-loan, OTC, own funds) for one block and faces no economic cost apart from gas.

## Proof of Code
// SPDX-License-Identifier: UNLICENSED
pragma solidity ^0.8.20;
import "forge-std/Test.sol";
import {PlumeStaking} from "src/PlumeStaking.sol";
import {StakingFacet} from "src/facets/StakingFacet.sol";
import {ValidatorFacet} from "src/facets/ValidatorFacet.sol";
import {MockPUSD as MockPLUME} from "src/mocks/MockPUSD.sol";

/*
   This is a **reduced** harness that deploys the logic contract directly (no diamond) so the
   percentage-check vulnerability can be executed in a single test.
*/
contract ValidatorPercentageBypass is Test {
    PlumeStaking staking;
    MockPLUME token;

    uint16 constant A = 1;
    uint16 constant B = 2;

    address alice = makeAddr("alice");    // delegate to validator A
    address bob   = makeAddr("bob");      // temporary capital provider
    address admin = makeAddr("admin");

    function setUp() public {
        token = new MockPLUME();
        staking = new PlumeStaking();
        staking.initializePlume(admin, 1e18, 1 days, 2 days, 5e26); // misc params

        vm.prank(admin);
        staking.setMaxValidatorPercentage(10 * 1e25);  // 10 %

        vm.prank(admin);
        staking.addValidator(A, 0, admin, admin, "", "", address(0), type(uint256).max);
        vm.prank(admin);
        staking.addValidator(B, 0, admin, admin, "", "", address(0), type(uint256).max);

        // fund users
        token.mint(alice, 200_000 ether);
        token.mint(bob,   9_000_000 ether);
        vm.prank(alice); token.approve(address(staking), type(uint256).max);
        vm.prank(bob);   token.approve(address(staking), type(uint256).max);
        // set PLUME token inside staking storage (mock) — omitted here for brevity
    }

    function test_Bypass() public {
        // Alice attempt without manipulation – should revert
        vm.prank(alice);
        vm.expectRevert();
        staking.stake(A, 200_000 ether);

        // Manipulation happens inside the same mined block
        vm.startPrank(bob);
        staking.stake(B, 9_000_000 ether);
        vm.stopPrank();

        vm.prank(alice);
        staking.stake(A, 200_000 ether); // now succeeds

        // Bob exits again
        vm.prank(bob);
        staking.unstake(B, 9_000_000 ether);

        // Validator A holds > 10 % of the real stake
        (uint256 stakeA,,,) = staking.getValidatorStats(A);
        uint256 total = staking.totalAmountStaked();
        assertGt(stakeA * 10, total, "cap bypassed – stakeA now exceeds 10% of total");
    }
}

## Suggested Mitigation
Perform the ratio check against the *post-stake, post-unstake* supply that includes a mandatory lock-up:

require( (validatorStake + amount) * PRECISION <= maxValidatorPercentage * (totalStaked + amount) , "cap" );

and additionally block an unstake that would make any validator exceed the percentage afterwards:

require( validatorStakeAfterUnstake * PRECISION <= maxValidatorPercentage * (totalStakedAfterUnstake), "cap" );

Because both staking and unstaking keep the invariant, a one-block inflation followed by immediate withdrawal can no longer leave the system in an invalid state. A TWAP is unnecessary – the invariant enforcement is simpler and cheaper.

## [M-42]. DOS issue in ValidatorFacet::slashValidator

## Description
The `slashValidator` function in `ValidatorFacet.sol` requires a unanimous vote from all registered validators to slash a malicious actor. The check `require(slashVoteCounts[validatorId] == $.totalValidators, "...")` enforces this. This design makes the slashing mechanism extremely brittle and prone to denial of service. A single inactive, offline, or malicious validator that refuses to vote can permanently prevent any slashing from occurring. An attacker could register their own validator and then go offline, effectively disabling the entire slashing security feature for the protocol.

## Impact
Because the unanimity requirement can be blocked by any single validator, malicious or offline, the slashing mechanism turns into a veto system. A validator that mis-behaves (double signs, censorship, etc.) can no longer be punished, greatly reducing the economic security that delegation-staking relies on. While this does not instantly steal user funds, it removes an essential deterrent and opens the door for prolonged malicious behaviour and collusion.

## Proof of Concept
1. Network is running with three validators (ids 1, 2, 3).
2. Validator 1 behaves maliciously.
